name: Queens Park Rangers Football Club
notes: QPR Holdings' 2024/25 group accounts on Companies House are a scanned PDF with no text layer: figures were read from the page images, so a script that extracts PDF text will not find the evidence phrases. Year end is 31 May. Operating loss (£20,793k) is before profit on player sales; the strategic report gives 'Group operating losses increased to £18m after player trading'. Companies House lists Ruben Gnanalingam (the ultimate owner of Total Soccer Growth Holdings; his row carries no separate stake) as the only active PSC of QPR Holdings with significant influence or control; Tony Fernandes ceased as PSC on 8 July 2023 and Amit Bhatia's directorship ended on 21 July 2026. The date QPR Newco LLC (Richard Reilly) first invested is not stated in the documents reviewed (Reilly became a director in February 2022). The group also carries non-convertible bonds of £7,047k (training-ground bond issue) and an EFL FFP settlement liability. The stadium is the Matrade Loftus Road Stadium (registered office name). The club's own site (qpr.co.uk) renders in the browser and could not be read, and web search ran out, so founding year, attendance, kit supplier and shirt sponsor are not filled. No valuation or social-follower count found. The club stays in the Championship for 2026/27 (club site season data). Ownership history (BBC Sport): Gnanalingam reached 33% in June 2016; Fernandes sold all his shares in July 2023; Bhatia agreed in July 2026 to transfer his stake to Gnanalingam (stake size not stated), which may supersede the 10.92% Sea Dream holding in the accounts' post-balance-sheet table. Capacity is as BBC Sport stated it in August 2018 (18,439); no newer official figure was found.

ownership_summary: The club company is wholly owned by QPR Holdings Limited. After Sea Dream Ltd (the L.N. Mittal family) transferred shares to Total Soccer Growth Holdings in June 2025 and £3.7m of shareholder loans were capitalised in October 2025, QPR Holdings is 78.94% owned by Total Soccer Growth Holdings Ltd (ultimately Ruben Gnanalingam), 10.92% by Sea Dream Ltd (the L.N. Mittal family) and 10.00% by QPR Newco LLC (ultimately Richard Reilly), with 0.14% held by minority shareholders. The three main shareholders fund the club through interest-free shareholder loans. In July 2026 director and co-owner Amit Bhatia (of the Mittal family side) agreed to transfer his stake to Gnanalingam, so the Sea Dream holding shown in the accounts may since have passed to him.
